title: JAKA Robotics Debuts Kargo50 Heavy-Duty Wheeled Humanoid and Zu50 Cobot at Shanghai Industry Fair
source_used: Pandaily (own report, citing Shanghai Securities News and Jiemian News)
key_facts: JAKA Robotics is using the 26th China International Industry Fair in Shanghai, which opens on 12 Oct 2026, to launch the JAKA Kargo50, a heavy-duty wheeled humanoid robot, and the JAKA Zu50, a high-payload collaborative robot; the company called both global debuts, according to Shanghai Securities News.

The Kargo50 extends JAKA's Kargo line of wheeled humanoids into heavier industrial work, chiefly moving totes and other materials between stations; JAKA has not published payload or other specifications for it.

JAKA says the smaller Kargo10 is in large-scale commercial use at automotive parts and high-end electronics factories; after on-site tuning its cycle time per tote fell from 105 to 28 seconds, and deployment in a new scenario takes 57 days.
The Zu50 tops JAKA's collaborative arm range: up to 50 kg payload, 2,100 mm reach and up to 50% higher axis speed, per JAKA's website product listing.
On the eve of the fair, Jiemian News watched two wheeled humanoids on JAKA's booth work as a pair: one carried an engine to a set position, the other tightened its screws.

JAKA's marketing lead Wang Lei called the booth setup an agent-driven collaborative system for new energy motors, running on JAKA EVO, the embodied intelligence operating system JAKA released in 2025.
JAKA was founded in 2014 and runs two product lines, collaborative robots and embodied intelligence.
quote_evidence: The company described both as global debuts, according to Shanghai Securities News.
JAKA has not yet published payload or other specifications for the new model, and the Kargo50 does not appear on the company's English product pages as of launch day.
JAKA says the Kargo10 is in large-scale commercial use at automotive parts and high-end electronics factories.
why_it_matters_hint: A Chinese maker is moving its wheeled humanoids from lighter work to heavier factory hauling, but the Kargo50 has no published specifications and the Kargo10 results are JAKA's own.
event_date: Launch at the fair opening on 12 Oct 2026
